newsitem.title: UK: Imperial, Gallaher sued by cancer sufferers.
newsitem.headline: Imperial, Gallaher sued by cancer sufferers.

text.p: Forty British cancer sufferers are planning to sue two tobacco companies for failing to change their products to limit the dangers of smoking, their lawyer said on Friday.

For the first time in a case of this size in Britain the plantiffs, who have been denied legal aid, will be represented by lawyers working on a no-win, no-fee basis. "These are cases which must and should be brought within the British legal system. It would be an outrage if because of the refusal of legal aid that these people couldn't bring their case to court," solicitor Martyn Day told BBC radio.

The cancer sufferers say Imperial Tobacco, being demerged from conglomerate Hanson Plc and Gallaher, a unit of American Brands of the United States, should have reduced levels of tar in cigarettes after it became clear 40 years ago that it was causing cancer.
The tobacco companies argue there is no proof that these people would not have suffered from cancer if the tar levels in the cigarettes had been reduced.
The lawyers will receive no fee if the cancer victims lose the case but could earn an estimated three million stg in fees and a similar amount from the plantiffs if they are successful.
The cancer victims were denied a petition for legal aid in July on the grounds that the case was unlikely to succeed.

"In the last 40 years, hundreds of such cases have been brought against tobacco companies worldwide and none of them have resulted in any tobacco company paying any damages at all," a spokesman for Imperial Tobacco said.

Jeff Jeffery, a spokesman for Gallaher, said: "The company's policy is not to comment on matters of litigation whether current or pending." The first step in the legal action is expected within the next few weeks and the case could reach court within two years. ($1=.6416 Pound)
